They use advanced evasion techniques, such as delayed execution and obfuscated payloads, to avoid detection.

attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the environment.

Payload decrypts and executes further code, establishes C2 communication, and exfiltrates host data.

attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution, further compromise, or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of subprocesses from utility or data formatting functions
Decryption and execution of embedded or remote code at runtime
Background threads launched on import in libraries
Endless polling of remote C2 servers for executable payloads
Exfiltration of host environment data (OS, MAC, working directory) to external servers
file_indicators: Presence of edt/bounding.py or similar hidden modules
Obfuscated or hex-encoded strings in code
network_indicators: HTTP POSTs with host profiling data
Polling for .jpg or other non-standard payloads from C2
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that spawn subprocesses or execute code from obfuscated strings, especially in utility functions. Flag packages that collect and exfiltrate host data or poll remote servers for executable payloads. Use static analysis to detect XOR/hex/Base64 decryption routines and dynamic analysis to catch delayed execution. Watch for network connections to known C2 domains/IPs and unusual HTTP POSTs from development environments.
